issues.description: Method addGuestStudents: the template defines addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) while the problem statement describes addGuestStudents(int) and the solution repository implements addGuestStudents(int). This parameter-list mismatch (extra boolean parameter in the template) will prevent students from implementing the method as specified and from matching the solution/tests, causing confusion and potential compilation/test failures.

The exercise requires a method to add guest students. The problem statement refers to addGuestStudents(int). The solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). The template, however, declares public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) (an extra boolean parameter). Although the method name is identical, the parameter lists differ, so students cannot directly implement the one-argument method expected by the problem/solution using the template stub; this mismatch can cause confusion or compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template signature with the problem statement and solution. Change the template method declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } . Alternatively, if input validation is desired, update the problem statement, template and solution consistently to document and implement the two-parameter signature (addGuestStudents(int, boolean)) and update tests accordingly.
